patterns: is australia a continent or a country
entries.answer: A continent is one of the seven large land masses on Earth, and the division is a convention rather than a law of nature, which is why the number has changed several times. The seven usually named are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, South America and Australia, and they hold all of the land that rises above sea level. Their boundaries follow lines that are practical rather than natural: the border between Asia and Europe runs along a river and a mountain range, and the line between North and South America cuts through a country rather than through empty ocean. Africa is the largest by area and Asia the largest by population, while Antarctica is the largest overall but has no permanent residents and almost entirely permanent ice. The other thing that makes continents uneven is that North America and Russia sit on the same landmass, so there is a continuous stretch of land from Alaska across to Asia with no ocean in between.

patterns: is the equator the hottest place
entries.answer: The equator is an imaginary circle around the middle of the Earth at zero degrees latitude that divides it into the northern and southern hemispheres, and it is the reference line from which latitude is measured. It is not actually the widest part of the planet: because the Earth is flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, the true widest circle, called the parallel of latitude, is a little further north, and the location of that maximum was one of the measurements that proved the flattening. Along the equator the sun is almost directly overhead at noon around the equinoxes, which is why equatorial regions get a strong and very regular daily cycle of day and night, and it is also why places near the equator are hot year round while places at the same latitude in the north are not. The line passes through nine countries and crosses the Indonesian island of Sumatra almost exactly.

entries.answer: A mountain is a landform that rises steeply above the surrounding land, and the interesting part is not that it is high but why it is high, since the two main causes produce completely different mountains. Volcanic mountains are built by material erupting from below and piling up around a vent, so they tend to be isolated, conical and comparatively young, and a very tall one like Everest is not one of them. Fold mountains come from the collision of two plates pushing up the crust, they form long chains along plate boundaries, and they are the reason the Himalaya and the Andes exist at all. Fault-block mountains are made when one block of crust is lifted along a fault while the land beside it drops, which is common in the western United States. Height is not the only variable: a mountain standing alone on a plain can be lower than one in a chain and still be a much harder climb, because a plateau gives no shelter and no approach. The Andes, the Himalaya, the Alps and the Cordillera are all fold systems, and the Cordillera runs the whole length of the western Americas.

patterns: difference between continental and volcanic island
entries.answer: An island is a body of land surrounded by water smaller than a continent, and the reason so many exist is that sea level has changed enormously over Earth's history, drowning land that used to be connected. Three broad types cover almost all of them. Continental islands sit on the edge of a continental shelf, are the part nearest the mainland, and are usually the largest: Great Britain separated from Europe when the North Sea flooded. Volcanic islands form where magma rises from the sea floor, and are usually small, young and curved in outline, like Hawaii, because a volcano that grows above water eventually stops rising and gets eroded away. Coral islands grow upward as the reef builds limestone on the skeleton of dead coral, and because coral needs warm shallow water they cluster in the tropics, which is why most of them are in the Pacific and Indian Oceans. The Philippines is entirely made of islands of these three kinds, which explains both its long coastline and its vulnerability to sea level rise.
